verdict_text:
YES

The script performs the shared-tensor verification first (identical key sets across all three, plus bit-exact equality of every non-MLP tensor against the base), computes each task vector against the untouched `base` dict (`out` is a separate shallow copy, and `base[name]` is never mutated in place), applies `b + 0.4*(f1-b) + 0.4*(f2-b)` in float32 before casting back to the base's float16 dtype, copies all other tensors from the base under unchanged names, and asserts both `merged == 64` and `len(out) == 244` before writing the single file to `out/T4/model.safetensors`. The regex is anchored with `fullmatch` and covers exactly the four MLP tensor names per layer, so no non-MLP tensor is captured; it does not bound the layer index to 0..15, but the `merged == 64` check would catch any surplus.

One thing I could not verify from reading alone: the script imports `load_checkpoint` from a local `_ckpt` module that is not part of the artifact shown, so its loading behaviour (e.g. that it returns the raw fp16 tensors of a single file) is assumed rather than confirmed.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
